_honest_cost: This is a REAL product loss: eight apps leave the catalogue, and jupyter and jellyfin are the two most likely to be missed. Nothing here claims they were replaced.
_signing: UNSIGNED BY CONSTRUCTION. Every entry carries "signature": "" and is inert until `make sign-registry` is run by the founder.
_source: registry.d/apt-retired.json — the eight still-enabled apt entries that CANNOT be expressed in the one install format, disabled with a per-app reason. Staged for the single writer of registry.json. See roadmap/INSTALL-METHODOLOGY.md §7.
_why_disabled_not_deleted: An entry that is refused at install time but still LISTED is the worse of the two failures: the App Hub offers a button that always errors. `_disabled` makes InstallFromRegistry refuse by name before anything else runs, and keeps the curated metadata (arch, keywords, icon, the reason) on disk so re-enabling any of these is one field, not a fresh investigation. Deleting them would throw away the only record of why they are gone.

cockpit._note: PARKED BY THE INSTALL-METHODOLOGY MIGRATION, 2026-08-17. cockpit is a Debian-integrated system component (cockpit-ws, -bridge, -system, -networkmanager, -storaged, -packagekit) that installs into /usr/lib and talks to systemd and PackageKit on the host. Upstream publishes no self-contained per-architecture artefact, so there is nothing to pin. If Vulos wants a Cockpit-like panel it belongs in the base image, not in a per-app catalogue that installs into $HOME/.vulos/apps. Its `install` shell string is left in place verbatim rather than blanked: the installer refuses it loudly (INSTALL-01) and the string is the record of what the app used to need. `_disabled` is what actually stops it, and it is reversible in one edit.

cockpit.description: Web-based server management — terminal, logs, processes, networking, storage, and system monitoring in one dashboard
cockpit.name: Cockpit

httpbin._note: PARKED BY THE INSTALL-METHODOLOGY MIGRATION, 2026-08-17. httpbin was `pip3 install --break-system-packages httpbin gunicorn`. pip is a package manager with the SAME unpinned-resolution problem as apt — `pip install httpbin` on two days gives two httpbins — so swapping one for the other would trade nothing. There is no single pinned artefact for a Python app plus its dependency tree, and building one is a wheel-bundling project, not a recipe edit. steam._note: PARKED BY THE INSTALL-METHODOLOGY MIGRATION, 2026-08-17. Removed from the catalogue by APP-CATALOG policy 1a (proprietary apps excluded, founder call 2026-08-15, explicitly reversible) — not by this migration. Also amd64-only on every vehicle (Debian's steam-installer and Flathub's com.valvesoftware.Steam alike), and its Flathub package is extra-data: a 35.5 MB download for a 52.5 MB install, i.e. a stub that fetches the real client from Valve. Disabled rather than deleted so reopening policy 1a is one edit. Its `install` shell string is left in place verbatim rather than blanked: the installer refuses it loudly (INSTALL-01) and the string is the record of what the app used to need. `_disabled` is what actually stops it, and it is reversible in one edit. PERMS-01 CORRECTION 2026-08-19: this recipe declared ['display', 'filesystem', 'network', 'gpu', 'audio'], and "display" and "audio" have never been Vulos permissions (backend/services/appnet/manifest.go). That was inert documentation until the Flatpak permission bridge landed; now an unrecognised string matches no enforced name, so the access it was meant to declare is REVOKED rather than granted. validateRecipeSecurity refuses the recipe outright (PERMS-01), which is why this entry could not be re-enabled even by accident. Corrected to the real strings; display and audio have no Vulos equivalent and are carried by the streaming lane, not by a permission. The entry stays _disabled under APP-CATALOG policy 1a regardless.
